presentation.defJa: いろいろなこと。いろいろと。
presentation.note: Common and neutral, suggesting thoughts or activity jumping among many things; いろいろ is broader and less vivid.
collocations: あれこれと世話を焼く

presentation.defJa: 電波を送ったり受けたりするための装置。
presentation.note: Also used figuratively, as in アンテナを張る, meaning to stay alert to trends and information.

presentation.meaning: suddenly, abruptly; straight away, without preliminaries
presentation.defJa: 前ぶれもなく、急に。順番をふまずに、すぐに。
presentation.note: Conversational and vivid, often implying that expected steps were skipped; 突然 is more neutral and suits formal writing.

presentation.meaning: many, several; how many (a prefix forming words for many layers, many times, many days)
presentation.defJa: ほかの言葉の前について、数が多いことや、はっきりしない数を表す。
presentation.note: A literary prefix found mainly in fixed compounds such as 幾重にも and 幾度となく; everyday speech uses 何度も or 何日も instead.

presentation.meaning: equal; equals, is the same as
presentation.defJa: 二つのものが同じであること。等しいこと。
presentation.note: Besides the math sign, it is used colloquially between two nouns to mean 'amounts to', as in AイコールB, and often in the negative イコールではない.
collocations: 必ずしもイコールではない

presentation.meaning: about every little thing; one by one
presentation.defJa: 一つ一つ全部。細かいことまでのこらず。
presentation.note: Often carries irritation, as in nitpicking every single thing; 一つ一つ is the neutral way to say one by one.

presentation.defJa: きのうの前の日。
presentation.note: Read いっさくじつ in formal speech such as press conferences, speeches and business correspondence; in everyday conversation the same characters are read おととい.
collocations: 一昨日お送りした資料

presentation.meaning: have a good day; see you later (polite send-off to someone leaving)
presentation.defJa: 出かける人を見送るときの、ていねいなあいさつ。無事に帰ってくることを願う気持ちがこもる。
presentation.note: The fuller, more polite form of 行ってらっしゃい, heard from older speakers and, with ませ added, in hotels, inns and shops.
collocations: 行っていらっしゃいませ
笑顔で行っていらっしゃいと送り出す
気をつけて行っていらっしゃい

presentation.meaning: I'm off; see you later (said when leaving home)
presentation.defJa: 家などから出かけるときに、残る人にかけるあいさつ。
presentation.note: Said by the person leaving, implying they will return, and answered with いってらっしゃい; often written 行ってきます.
collocations: いってきますと家を出る
いってきますのあいさつ

presentation.meaning: I'm off now; see you later (humble, more polite form)
presentation.defJa: 出かけるときに言う、へりくだったていねいなあいさつ。
presentation.note: The humble keigo version of いってきます, used at work, toward superiors or customers, and in formal speech; often written 行ってまいります.
collocations: 取引先へいってまいります
では、いってまいります
いってまいりますと頭を下げる

presentation.meaning: have a good day; see you later (said to someone leaving)
presentation.defJa: 出かける人を見送るときに言うあいさつ。
presentation.note: The everyday contracted form of 行っていらっしゃい, said by the person staying behind in reply to いってきます.
collocations: 行ってらっしゃいと見送る
気をつけて行ってらっしゃい
笑顔で行ってらっしゃいと言う

presentation.meaning: at last, finally (something long awaited is about to happen); more and more
presentation.defJa: 待っていたことが、とうとう始まろうとするようす。また、ますます。
presentation.note: Builds anticipation of an approaching event, whereas ついに and とうとう often mark something already reached; it can also mean 'increasingly'.

presentation.defJa: 印刷や筆記に使う、色のついた液体。インクの古い言い方。
presentation.note: An older form of インク that survives mainly in industry terms such as 印刷インキ and in company names; everyday speech uses インク.

presentation.meaning: woman (mainly in compounds such as career woman, businesswoman)
presentation.defJa: 女の人。多くはほかの言葉と組み合わせて使う。
presentation.note: Rarely used on its own; it appears in loan compounds like キャリアウーマン, which now sound somewhat dated, while 女性 is the normal word.

presentation.defJa: 羊の毛。また、それで作った糸や布。
presentation.note: The everyday word for wool fabric and clothing; 羊毛 is the more technical term for the raw fiber.

presentation.defJa: 喫茶店やレストランで、注文を聞いたり料理を運んだりする女性の店員。
presentation.note: Also spelled ウェイトレス; many businesses now prefer gender-neutral terms such as ホールスタッフ or simply 店員.
collocations: 喫茶店のウエートレス
ウエートレスとして働く

presentation.meaning: to appear (in a photo), to be photographed; to show through
presentation.defJa: 写真などに、姿や形がとらえられて現れる。また、裏や下にあるものが透けて見える。
presentation.note: Intransitive partner of 写す; use 写る for appearing in photos or showing through paper, and 映る for reflections and images on a mirror, water or screen.

presentation.defJa: 小麦粉をこねて、太く長く切った白いめん。
presentation.note: Thicker and chewier than soba, usually written in kana (kanji 饂飩 is rare), and served hot or cold in many regional styles.

presentation.meaning: to nod (in agreement or to show one is listening)
presentation.defJa: 相手の話に同意したり、聞いていることを示したりするために、首を縦に軽く振る。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (頷く is the kanji form); it covers both agreeing and simply showing you are following, and conversation advice often pairs it with 相づちを打つ.

presentation.meaning: presence or absence; whether or not something exists
presentation.defJa: あるかないかということ。
presentation.note: A formal noun common in forms, rules and news (アレルギーの有無, 経験の有無); 有無を言わせず is a separate idiom meaning forcibly, without giving any choice.

presentation.meaning: upper, outer (prefix in compounds such as the words for jacket, indoor shoes and overwriting)
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、「うえの方の」「外側の」という意味を加える。
presentation.note: The うわ reading appears only in fixed compounds such as 上着, 上履き, 上書き and 上回る, where it marks the upper or outer layer; elsewhere 上 is usually read うえ, じょう or かみ.

presentation.meaning: a lot, very much, a great deal
presentation.defJa: 量や程度がとても大きいようす。たくさん。
presentation.note: Casual and spoken, typical of advice from parents or elders; more colloquial than たくさん or ずっと, and it can also intensify comparisons (うんと大きい).

presentation.meaning: um, er, let me see (hesitation filler)
presentation.defJa: 言葉に詰まったときや、次に言うことを考えているときに口にする言葉。
presentation.note: A spoken filler used while recalling or working something out (ええと、何だっけ), whereas あのー more often softens an opening toward the listener; ええとですね sounds softer and politer in business talk.

presentation.defJa: 人に不快な思いをさせないために守るべき礼儀や作法。
presentation.note: Close to マナー, but エチケット leans toward personal courtesy that spares others discomfort, and it appears in set phrases like 咳エチケット and エチケット袋.

presentation.defJa: 料理や作業のときに、服が汚れないよう体の前に着ける布。
presentation.note: A loanword fully at home in everyday Japanese; エプロン姿 is a common image of someone cooking or working in a shop, while 前掛け is the older native word.

presentation.defJa: 弦楽器・管楽器・打楽器などを、多くの奏者でいっしょに演奏する大きな楽団。
presentation.note: Usually means a Western symphony orchestra; 管弦楽団 is the formal equivalent used in ensemble names, and 楽団 is the broader word for any band.
collocations: オーケストラを指揮する

presentation.defJa: 機械やコンピューターを使い、人の手を使わずに作業や生産を自動で行うこと。
presentation.note: Somewhat dated and tied to factory lines; current writing prefers 自動化, while オートメーション survives in compounds like ファクトリーオートメーション.
collocations: 工場のオートメーション
オートメーションが進む

presentation.defJa: 機械をなめらかに動かしたり、料理や肌の手入れに使ったりする油。
presentation.note: Used for engine, lubricating, cosmetic and Western cooking oils (オリーブオイル), while 油 is the general native word; crude oil in economic news is usually 原油 or 石油.

presentation.defJa: 細かいところまで気にせず、全体をだいたいでとらえるようす。
presentation.note: Often written 大雑把; neutral for estimates and summaries (おおざっぱに言えば), but mildly critical when describing a person's sloppy character.

presentation.defJa: 「座ってください」をていねいに言う言葉。
presentation.note: Respectful form of 座ってください, from 腰を掛ける; standard in clinics, offices and interviews, where guests traditionally wait for this phrase before sitting down.
collocations: どうぞおかけください
こちらにおかけください
おかけになってお待ちください

presentation.meaning: thanks to you; fortunately (polite reply about one's health or circumstances)
presentation.defJa: 相手や周りの人の助けに感謝しながら、無事であることやうまくいったことを伝えるあいさつ。
presentation.note: A polite social formula used even when the listener did nothing specific; businesses also use it to preface good news, while plain おかげで can turn sarcastic.
collocations: おかげさまで元気です
おかげさまで好評です

presentation.meaning: dish eaten with rice; side dish
presentation.defJa: ご飯といっしょに食べる料理。肉や魚、野菜などを使ったもの。
presentation.note: The everyday word for anything eaten with rice, from main dishes to small sides; 副菜 is the nutrition term for vegetable side dishes specifically.

presentation.meaning: please don't go to any trouble (for me)
presentation.defJa: 自分のために特別な気づかいやもてなしをしなくてよい、と相手に伝える言葉。
presentation.note: A guest's polite formula from 構う (to attend to someone), usually answered by the host insisting anyway; it can also brush off unwanted concern.
collocations: おかまいなく、すぐ失礼します

presentation.defJa: 朝、人に会ったときに言う、くだけたあいさつの言葉。
presentation.note: The casual short form of おはようございます, used with family, friends and juniors; in TV and entertainment work the full form is used to greet colleagues at any hour.

presentation.meaning: sorry to have kept you waiting
presentation.defJa: 相手を待たせたことをわびて、ていねいに言う言葉。
presentation.note: The standard polite apology for a wait in service, announcements and business; お待たせ is the casual form among friends, and おまちどおさま sounds older and homier.
collocations: 大変お待たせしました
長らくお待たせしました
お待たせしました、こちらがご注文の品です

presentation.defJa: 「待ってください」をていねいに言う言葉。
presentation.note: A respectful request standard in shops, phone calls and announcements; 少々お待ちくださいませ is even more deferential, while ちょっと待って is the casual equivalent.
collocations: しばらくお待ちください
このままお待ちください

presentation.meaning: sorry to have kept you waiting (casual, homely)
presentation.defJa: 待たせた相手に、親しみを込めて言うあいさつ。食べ物を出すときなどに使う。
presentation.note: An older, folksy expression typical of soba shops and delivery; warmer but less formal than お待たせしました, and rarely heard in corporate service.
collocations: おまちどおさまでした

presentation.defJa: 祝うのにふさわしいようす。喜ばしい。
presentation.note: Mostly used for celebratory events (おめでたい席), but said of a person it means naively optimistic, and the noun おめでた often refers to a pregnancy.

presentation.defJa: 食事と食事の間に食べる軽い食べ物。特に午後に食べるお菓子など。
presentation.note: A warm, homely word for a between-meal treat, especially for children; 間食 is the neutral term used in health contexts.

presentation.defJa: 鍵盤を押し、空気でリードやパイプを鳴らして音を出す楽器。
presentation.note: In Japan it often evokes the school reed organ (足踏みオルガン), while church and concert-hall instruments are usually specified as パイプオルガン.

presentation.meaning: honorific prefix showing respect (as in the formal spoken word for "your company")
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、相手や相手に関係するものへの敬意を表す語。
presentation.note: The おん reading is formal and limited to fixed words like 御社, 御中 and 御礼; the same kanji is far more often read お or ご (御飯, 御意見).

presentation.defJa: 夏に多い小さな虫で、雌が人や動物の血を吸う。かゆみや病気の原因になる。
presentation.note: An everyday word; a bite is normally 蚊に刺される in standard Japanese (噛まれる is regional), and 蚊の鳴くような声 is a common idiom for a faint, tiny voice.

presentation.defJa: 道や線などが弓のように曲がっているところ。また、野球で曲がりながら進む球。
presentation.note: Common for road and rail bends and in baseball, and usable as a verb (カーブする); 曲がり角 suggests a sharper corner rather than a sweeping bend.

presentation.defJa: かたいからを持つ、海や川にすむ生き物。また、そのから。
presentation.note: Covers both the living shellfish, as food or in ecology, and the shell itself, though 貝殻 is used when the empty shell is meant specifically.

presentation.meaning: each, every (prefix: every region, each country, each person)
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、「それぞれの」「一つ一つの」という意味を表す。
presentation.note: A formal prefix common in news and official writing (各地, 各国, 各社) that attaches to Sino-Japanese nouns, while それぞれ is the everyday equivalent.

presentation.defJa: ある数を、もう一つの数の回数だけ足し合わせる計算。
presentation.note: Usually written 掛け算 or, in schoolbooks, かけ算; it is the everyday word, while 乗法 is the formal mathematical term.

presentation.meaning: to repeat, accumulate (efforts, experience); to pile up, stack
presentation.defJa: ものの上に同じようなものを置く。また、同じことを何度も繰り返す。
presentation.note: Beyond stacking objects, it very often means repeating or accumulating effort over time (改良を重ねる, 回を重ねる), with a sense of steady build-up that 繰り返す lacks.

presentation.defJa: 見た目を美しくするために付けたり置いたりするもの。
presentation.note: The everyday native word for decorations (クリスマスの飾り, 正月飾り); 装飾 is the more formal written equivalent, and 飾り気がない describes an unpretentious person.

presentation.meaning: certainly; understood (polite, humble acknowledgment of a request)
presentation.defJa: 「わかりました」をとても丁寧に言う言葉。客や目上の人の頼みを受けるときに使う。
presentation.note: The standard service-industry reply to a customer's request and a polite reply to a superior; slightly more deferential than 承知しました, and far more polite than 分かりました.
collocations: はい、かしこまりました
かしこまりました、少々お待ちください
ご注文、かしこまりました

presentation.meaning: spot, place, section (a particular point in a location or a text)
presentation.defJa: ある特定の場所や部分。文章の一部分を指すこともある。
presentation.note: Normally written 箇所 (also 個所) and counted with ～か所; a formal word common in news, reports and proofreading, more specific than 所 or 場所.
collocations: 誤りのある箇所を直す

presentation.meaning: to gnaw, to bite into (something hard); to dabble in (a subject)
presentation.defJa: 硬い物を歯で少しずつかみ取る。物事を少しだけ学ぶという意味もある。
presentation.note: Describes biting small pieces off something hard such as an apple, nut or pencil; figuratively it means having only a smattering of a subject, and 親のすねをかじる means living off one's parents.
collocations: フランス語を少しかじる

presentation.meaning: cassette (especially an audio cassette tape); snap-in cartridge
presentation.defJa: 録音用のテープなどを、出し入れしやすいようにプラスチックのケースに収めたもの。
presentation.note: Today mostly heard in カセットテープ and in カセットコンロ or ガスカセット, where it means any snap-in cartridge such as a gas canister.

presentation.meaning: katakana (the angular Japanese syllabary used mainly for loanwords)
presentation.defJa: 日本語の文字の一つ。主に外来語や擬音語を書くのに使う、角ばった形の文字。
presentation.note: In running text it is usually written カタカナ or 片仮名; カタカナ語 refers to loanwords, whose overuse is a perennial topic of language commentary.

presentation.meaning: to be tidied up, be put in order; to be settled, be finished
presentation.defJa: 散らかっていた物がきちんと整う。また、問題や仕事が終わる。
presentation.note: Intransitive partner of 片付ける (to tidy something up); usually written 片付く, and used for work or problems being dealt with as well as for rooms.

presentation.defJa: 学校などで、決められた順序で学ぶ内容や期間のまとまり。
presentation.note: Refers to a structured program of study such as 修士課程 or 教職課程; don't confuse it with the homophone 過程, which means process.

presentation.meaning: (large hanging) bell, especially a temple bell
presentation.defJa: 寺などにつるし、太い棒でついて鳴らす大きな金属の器具。
presentation.note: Usually a large struck bell such as a temple or church bell, whereas 鈴 is a small jingling bell and ベル an electric or hand bell.

presentation.meaning: cover (e.g., a paper book cover or protective case); also, making up for a shortfall
presentation.defJa: 物を包んだり覆ったりして守るもの。本の表紙を包む紙など。
presentation.note: As a noun it means a protective covering for a book, sofa or phone; as カバーする it is very common for covering for someone or making up for a loss or gap.

presentation.defJa: 湿った所で、食べ物や壁などに生える小さな菌。
presentation.note: Usually written カビ in katakana (the kanji 黴 is rare); the standard verb is 生える, and カビ臭い describes a musty smell.

presentation.defJa: 口の中でかんで味わい、飲み込まずに捨てる菓子。
presentation.note: Short for チューインガム; the verb is かむ, and chewing it in meetings or while serving customers is still widely seen as rude in Japan.

presentation.meaning: song, ballad; popular song (mostly in compounds, for Showa-era Japanese pop)
presentation.defJa: 多くの人に親しまれ、広く歌われる歌。特に昭和の流行歌を指すことが多い。
presentation.note: Rarely used alone; it mostly appears in compounds such as 歌謡曲 and 昭和歌謡, evoking mainstream Japanese pop from before the J-pop era.

presentation.meaning: shell, husk (of an egg, nut, shellfish, etc.)
presentation.defJa: 卵や貝、木の実などの外側を包んでいる硬いもの。
presentation.note: Used for eggs, nuts and shellfish, and figuratively in 殻を破る (break out of one's shell) and 殻に閉じこもる (withdraw into oneself).
collocations: 自分の殻に閉じこもる

presentation.meaning: color (as in color TV or color printing); also, collar
presentation.defJa: 色。白黒ではなく、色がついていること。
presentation.note: カラー usually means colour in loanword compounds and product terms (カラー印刷, スクールカラー) while everyday colour is 色; the homophone meaning collar appears mainly in ホワイトカラー and ブルーカラー.

presentation.meaning: to tease, to make fun of
presentation.defJa: 冗談を言ったりして、相手を困らせたり笑いものにしたりする。
presentation.note: Ranges from playful teasing to mean-spirited ridicule depending on context; more casual than 嘲る and milder than ばかにする.

presentation.meaning: karuta (traditional Japanese card game, esp. the poem-matching game)
presentation.defJa: 読み上げられた札に合う札を取り合う、日本の伝統的なカードの遊び。
presentation.note: Associated with New Year family play and with 百人一首, the 100-poem set used in competitive karuta; it may also be written カルタ.

presentation.meaning: to dry (something), e.g. laundry or hair
presentation.defJa: ぬれている物から水分を取り除いて、水気をなくす。
presentation.note: Transitive verb for actively drying something; its intransitive partner is 乾く (to become dry).

presentation.defJa: 物と物、または出来事と出来事の間のへだたり。
presentation.note: Covers both physical spacing and time intervals; common in notices such as 間隔を空けてお並びください.

presentation.defJa: いつまでと前もって決められた日や時間の区切り。
presentation.note: A fixed cutoff set by rules or contracts (提出期限, 有効期限); 締め切り is the more everyday word for a submission deadline.

presentation.defJa: 暴力や犯罪を行う集団。また、その一員。
presentation.note: Usually evokes American-style organized crime, especially in films; Japanese organized crime is called 暴力団 or ヤクザ instead.

presentation.defJa: 仕事や活動をやめて、体や心を休めること。
presentation.note: A somewhat formal word used in health and labor contexts (休息時間, 休息が必要だ); 休み and 休憩 are the everyday words for a break.

presentation.defJa: 財産を個人ではなく社会全体のものにしようとする考え方。主に「主義」「党」などと組み合わせて使う。
presentation.note: Almost never used alone; it appears in political and historical compounds like 共産主義 (communism), 共産党 (Communist Party) and 共産圏 (the communist bloc).

presentation.defJa: 細長い木の胴に十三本の弦を張った、日本の伝統的な弦楽器。
presentation.note: Read こと on its own; the on-reading きん appears in compounds such as 琴線 (きんせん, heartstrings) and 木琴 (もっきん, xylophone).

presentation.defJa: 部屋の空気を冷やす機械。
presentation.note: A slightly old-fashioned everyday word for a cooling air conditioner; エアコン is now more common, and クーラーボックス means a portable cooler box.

presentation.defJa: 鼻がむずむずして、急に息を強く吐き出すこと。
presentation.note: Usually written in hiragana; the natural verbs are 出る and する, and it often comes up alongside 鼻水 in talk of colds and hay fever.
collocations: くしゃみが止まらない

presentation.defJa: 価値がなく、取るに足りない。ばかばかしい。
presentation.note: Often harshly dismissive (くだらない！ for 'Rubbish!'), but between friends it can be affectionate, as in くだらない話 meaning silly, idle chatter.
collocations: くだらないことでけんかする

presentation.meaning: to go down, to descend (a river, slope, etc.)
presentation.defJa: 高い所から低い所へ移る。川の流れに沿って進む。
presentation.note: Used for travelling down rivers, slopes and mountains, and figuratively for decisions handed down from above (判決が下る); the opposite of 上る.

presentation.meaning: to stick to, to cling to
presentation.defJa: 物と物がぴったりついて、離れなくなる。
presentation.note: Casual, vivid counterpart of 付着する; it is also used for people who stay close together or who start dating (二人がくっつく).

presentation.defJa: 物を他の物にぴったりつけて、離れないようにする。
presentation.note: Casual transitive partner of くっつく; in writing, 貼る (to stick something flat) or 付ける is often more precise.

presentation.defJa: 店にお金を払って衣類などを洗ってもらうこと。また、その店。
presentation.note: Normally means professional laundry or dry cleaning, not cleaning in general, which is 掃除; ハウスクリーニング is a hired home-cleaning service.

presentation.meaning: to wrap up snugly, to envelop
presentation.defJa: 布などで全体をおおうように包みこむ。
presentation.note: Softer and more colloquial than 包む, くるむ suggests rolling something soft all the way around an object, like a blanket around a baby or foil around food.

presentation.defJa: 都道府県の中で、いくつかの町や村をまとめた地域の区分。
presentation.note: Today a 郡 is mostly a geographic label in the addresses of towns and villages; cities never belong to one, and 郡部 refers to rural areas as opposed to 市部.

presentation.defJa: 名詞の前について、今の、今その地位にあるという意味を表す。
presentation.note: Attached to nouns in formal writing, especially news, to mark the current holder or state (現首相, 現住所), in contrast to 元 or 前 for former ones.

presentation.defJa: 黒と白の石を交互に盤に置き、囲んだ陣地の広さを争う遊び。
presentation.note: 囲碁 is the standard full name in news and formal contexts, while 碁 appears in set phrases like 碁を打つ and in compounds such as 碁盤 and 碁石.

presentation.defJa: 言葉の前について、ちいさい、わずかな、という意味を加える。
presentation.note: Read こ in native-style compounds such as 小声, 小雨 and 小走り, unlike the Sino-Japanese しょう in words like 小学校, and it often adds a nuance of "slightly" as well as "small".

presentation.defJa: 決められた道筋。また、段階を追って進む学習の内容や順序。
presentation.note: Covers routes (race or hiking courses), programs (研修コース) and meals (フルコース) much as in English, and also a lane in swimming or track (第三コース).

presentation.defJa: 大勢で声を合わせて歌うこと。また、そのための集まり。
presentation.note: Used for amateur choirs and for backing vocals in pop music, while 合唱 is the more formal word used for school competitions and classical choral works.

presentation.defJa: 言葉の前について、程度や水準が上であることを表す。
presentation.note: Attaches mainly to Sino-Japanese nouns to mean "high" (高品質, 高水準), with 低 as its opposite, and is common in technical and economic writing.

presentation.defJa: このようにして。前に述べたことを受けて、その結果を示す。
presentation.note: Common in narratives and explanations to sum up a process and lead into its outcome, a little more conversational than このようにして.

presentation.defJa: 学校で授業などに使う建物。
presentation.note: Refers specifically to a school's buildings, whereas 校庭 is the grounds and 学校 the institution as a whole.

presentation.defJa: かたよりがなく、正しいこと。
presentation.note: Stresses impartial treatment under rules, as in courts, markets and elections, whereas 公平 focuses on giving everyone equal shares or equal treatment.

presentation.defJa: 秋に葉が赤く色づくカエデの木。また、秋に木の葉が赤や黄色に変わること。
presentation.note: Both readings are written 紅葉: こうよう is the general word for leaves turning color in autumn, while もみじ usually means the maple tree itself or its red leaves, as in もみじ狩り.

presentation.defJa: その人がどの国の国民であるかという身分。
presentation.note: Normally written in kanji as 国籍, it is the legal status of belonging to a country, distinct from 出身 (where one comes from) or 民族 (ethnicity).

presentation.meaning: to make, to prepare (often by hand)
presentation.defJa: 手間をかけて作り上げる。また、口実や話などを都合よく作る。
presentation.note: A somewhat old-fashioned, homely word for making things by hand, such as food or clothes, warmer than 作る, and it can also mean to make up an excuse or a story.

presentation.meaning: thank you for the meal (said after eating)
presentation.defJa: 食事を終えたときに、作ってくれた人や食べ物に感謝して言うあいさつ。
presentation.note: The polite ごちそうさまでした is the standard after-meal phrase, paired with いただきます before eating, and it is also said jokingly after someone gushes about their partner.
collocations: 手を合わせてごちそうさま

presentation.meaning: likewise; it is I who should say so (in reply to thanks or an apology)
presentation.defJa: 相手のお礼やおわびに対して、自分のほうも同じ気持ちだと返すことば。
presentation.note: Used only as a reply, turning the other person's thanks, apology or greeting (よろしく) back toward them, and it works in both polite business speech and casual talk.
collocations: こちらこそよろしくお願いします
こちらこそありがとうございました
こちらこそすみません

presentation.meaning: cook, chef (esp. of Western food); tap, stopcock
presentation.defJa: レストランなどで料理を作ることを仕事にしている人。特に西洋料理の料理人。
presentation.note: From Dutch kok, it means a professional cook of Western-style food and sounds slightly old-fashioned beside シェフ or 料理人, while a separate コック from English cock means a valve or tap, as in ガスのコック.

presentation.defJa: 人に知られないように、静かに何かをするようす。
presentation.note: An everyday word for doing something quietly so others will not notice, often harmless or playful, whereas ひそかに is more literary and 内緒で stresses keeping something secret.

presentation.defJa: 少し前のある日。最近。
presentation.note: A casual spoken contraction of この間 (このあいだ), common in conversation and relaxed essays but avoided in formal writing.
collocations: こないだはありがとう

presentation.defJa: 木の樹液や石油から作られる、よく伸び縮みする素材。
presentation.note: From Dutch gom, it is the everyday word for rubber and appears in many compounds such as 輪ゴム (rubber band) and 消しゴム (eraser), while ラバー is mostly technical or sports jargon.

presentation.meaning: excuse me, is anyone home? (called out when visiting)
presentation.defJa: よその家や店をたずねたとき、入り口で中の人に呼びかけることば。
presentation.note: A polite, somewhat old-fashioned call used at someone's entrance or a small shop to announce yourself, and among older speakers it can also mean goodbye at the end of a phone call.
collocations: ごめんくださいと声をかける

presentation.defJa: 趣味や研究のために、ある種類の物を集めること。また、集めた物。
presentation.note: Used for gathered items, from a museum's holdings to a hobbyist's stamps, and also for a fashion designer's seasonal line (春夏コレクション).
collocations: コレクションを公開する

presentation.defJa: 言葉の前について、「この」「現在の」という意味を表す。
presentation.note: Read こん before Sino-Japanese words and some loanwords in news and formal speech (今世紀, 今国会, 今シーズン), while everyday words like 今年 and 今朝 have readings of their own.

presentation.meaning: competition, contest (esp. in music or art)
presentation.defJa: 音楽や絵画などの作品や演技の出来を競い合う会。
presentation.note: From French concours, it is used for judged contests in music, art and design, while コンテスト is broader and 大会 is the usual word for sports.
collocations: コンクールに出場する
コンクールで入賞する

presentation.defJa: セメントに砂や砂利、水を混ぜて固めた建築材料。
presentation.note: Both an everyday and a technical word, with 鉄筋コンクリート meaning reinforced concrete, and it can also suggest a cold, artificial cityscape (コンクリートジャングル).
collocations: コンクリートを流し込む

presentation.defJa: 電気器具のプラグを差しこんで、電気を取るための差し込み口。
presentation.note: A Japan-made usage for a wall socket, unrelated to English "consent" except in the medical loanword インフォームド・コンセント.
collocations: コンセントに差し込む

presentation.defJa: 夜、人に会ったときに言うあいさつのことば。
presentation.note: Written with は (pronounced wa) because it comes from 今晩は, and it is used with people outside one's household rather than with family.
collocations: こんばんはと声をかける

presentation.meaning: club, circle (esp. an informal student club)
presentation.defJa: 同じ趣味や関心を持つ人たちが集まって活動する仲間の集まり。
presentation.note: At universities a サークル is a casual, student-run group, in contrast to the more formal and demanding 部 or 部活動.

presentation.defJa: 言葉の前について、「もう一度」「ふたたび」の意味を表す。
presentation.note: Attaches to Sino-Japanese action nouns to mean doing something again (再開, 再確認), and is highly productive in news and business Japanese.

presentation.defJa: 言葉の前について、「いちばん」「もっとも」の意味を表す。
presentation.note: Forms superlatives with Sino-Japanese nouns (最新, 最大, 最優先), more compact and formal than もっとも or いちばん.

presentation.defJa: 危険や緊急を知らせるために、高く長い音を出す装置。また、その音。
presentation.note: Used for ambulances, fire engines, police cars and disaster warnings, usually with 鳴る, 鳴らす or 鳴り響く.

presentation.meaning: to stick into, to get stuck (of a thorn, bone, etc.)
presentation.defJa: とがった物の先が、ほかの物の中に入って抜けなくなる。
presentation.note: The intransitive partner of 刺す; it is also used figuratively for words that hit home, and in recent slang for something that strongly resonates with you.

presentation.defJa: ぐずぐずしないで、手早く物事をするようす。
presentation.note: Casual, and often carries a brusque or impatient tone (さっさとしなさい), unlike the neutral すばやく or 手早く.

presentation.defJa: 人と別れるときに言うあいさつの言葉。
presentation.note: Sounds formal and somewhat final, so adults usually prefer じゃあね, またね or お先に失礼します in daily life; さよなら is the shorter, softer form.
collocations: さようならと手を振る

presentation.defJa: 会社などに勤めて、給料をもらって生活している人。
presentation.note: A made-in-Japan English word that usually pictures a male office worker; 会社員 is the neutral, gender-free term used in official writing.

presentation.meaning: refreshing, fresh, crisp (of air, breeze, manner)
presentation.defJa: すがすがしくて、気持ちがよいようす。
presentation.note: Describes weather, breezes, tastes and people's manner alike (さわやかな青年) with a sense of clean freshness, whereas 涼しい primarily refers to cool temperature.

presentation.defJa: 水溶液のpHが7より小さく、すっぱい性質を示すこと。
presentation.note: Contrasts with アルカリ性 (alkaline) and 中性 (neutral); common in science writing and on labels such as 弱酸性 skin cleansers.

presentation.meaning: season (period when an activity is at its peak)
presentation.defJa: あることが盛んに行われる時期。特に、スポーツの試合が行われる期間。
presentation.note: Usually means the period when an activity peaks (受験シーズン, 花粉シーズン); 季節 is the usual word for one of the four natural seasons.

presentation.defJa: 布団やベッドの上に敷く、大きな布。
presentation.note: Refers to bed sheets specifically; a sheet of paper or plastic is 紙 or シート, not シーツ.

presentation.defJa: 物音ひとつせず、とても静かなようす。
presentation.note: A drawn-out, more emphatic form of しんと (also written しーんと), usually paired with 静まり返る or なる when a room or crowd suddenly goes dead quiet.

presentation.meaning: square, four-cornered (as a noun: a square)
presentation.defJa: 四つの角があり、正方形や長方形のような形をしているようす。
presentation.note: Normally written 四角 (noun) and 四角い (adjective) in kanji; 四角四面 describes someone overly rigid and formal.

presentation.defJa: 春・夏・秋・冬の四つの季節。
presentation.note: A slightly formal word common in essays and tourism writing; 四季折々 (each season in turn) is a frequent set phrase.

presentation.defJa: 空気や物の中に含まれている水分。しめりけ。
presentation.note: In everyday speech this word is more often read しっけ; it means unwanted dampness you feel, while 湿度 is the measured humidity level.

presentation.defJa: 空気の中にどれくらい水蒸気が含まれているかを表す割合。
presentation.note: A measurable quantity usually given in percent; for the vague feeling of dampness Japanese use 湿気 instead.

presentation.defJa: 動物の体の後ろの端から細長く伸びている部分。
presentation.note: An everyday word, more colloquial than 尾; idioms include しっぽをつかむ (catch someone out) and しっぽを巻いて逃げる (flee with one's tail between one's legs).

presentation.defJa: その人が実際に持っている能力や力。
presentation.note: Stresses real, demonstrated ability rather than reputation or credentials; 実力主義 is a merit-based system, while 実力行使 means the use of force.

presentation.meaning: Excuse me (said on leaving); I'm sorry (for my rudeness)
presentation.defJa: 目上の人の部屋を出るときや、相手に迷惑をかけたことをわびるときに言う言葉。
presentation.note: The past form of 失礼します, said on leaving a teacher's or superior's room or when apologizing for a small slip; usually written 失礼しました, and more formal than すみません.
collocations: 先ほどは失礼しました

presentation.meaning: to go numb, to fall asleep (of a limb); to be thrilled
presentation.defJa: 体の一部の感覚がなくなり、じんじんして思うように動かなくなる。
presentation.note: Besides physical numbness it is used colloquially for being thrilled (演奏にしびれる), and the idiom しびれを切らす means to run out of patience.

presentation.meaning: to wither, to wilt; to deflate
presentation.defJa: ふくらんでいたものや開いていた花が、小さく縮んで元気がなくなる。
presentation.note: Used for flowers, balloons and, figuratively, for hopes or demand shrinking (景気がしぼむ); 枯れる means to dry up and die, while しぼむ is wilting or deflating.

presentation.meaning: to become damp, to be moist
presentation.defJa: 水分を含んで、少しぬれた状態になる。
presentation.note: Normally written 湿る; it means slightly damp rather than soaked (ぬれる), and should not be confused with the homophones 閉める and 締める.

presentation.defJa: 新聞や雑誌、テレビなどのために取材をして、記事や報道をつくる人。
presentation.note: Broader and weightier-sounding than 記者 (reporter); it often implies an independent writer or commentator rather than a staff member of one paper.
collocations: フリージャーナリスト
ジャーナリストとして活動する

presentation.defJa: ひざを深く曲げて腰を落とし、低い姿勢になる。
presentation.note: Means squatting low on one's heels, unlike 座る (to sit); しゃがみ込む stresses sinking down and staying there, often from fatigue or distress.

presentation.defJa: 横隔膜がけいれんして、ひくっという音とともに急に息を吸い込んでしまう現象。
presentation.note: The everyday word for hiccups, used with 出る and 止まる; the medical term 吃逆 appears only in clinical writing.
collocations: しゃっくりが止まらない

presentation.meaning: to suck on (a finger, candy, etc.)
presentation.defJa: 口の中に入れて、なめたり吸ったりする。
presentation.note: Implies repeatedly sucking or licking something held in the mouth, like a thumb or candy; 骨までしゃぶる figuratively means to exploit someone completely.

presentation.defJa: グー・チョキ・パーの三つの手の形を同時に出して、勝ち負けを決める遊び。
presentation.note: Used far more than in English-speaking countries to settle everyday decisions; the call is じゃんけんぽん, and a tie triggers あいこでしょ.

presentation.meaning: heavy-, serious- (as in heavy industry, heavy labor)
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、おもい、または程度がはなはだしいという意味を表す。
presentation.note: Read じゅう in Sino-Japanese compounds such as 重労働 and 重装備, and often paired with its opposite 軽 (軽工業 vs 重工業).

presentation.defJa: 病気やけがが重く、命が危ない状態。
presentation.note: A news-report term ranked above 重傷 (serious injury) for a life-threatening state; some papers write it 重態.

presentation.defJa: 床に敷く、毛などで織った厚い敷物。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana since the kanji 絨毯 is hard; カーペット is the more common everyday word, while じゅうたん evokes thick, often patterned rugs.

presentation.meaning: first-, initial- (as in first meeting, first day)
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、はじめての、または一番はじめのという意味を表す。
presentation.note: Read しょ in compounds such as 初対面, 初日 and 初年度, but はつ in words like 初雪 and 初出場, so the reading depends on the compound.

presentation.meaning: various, the many (as in foreign countries, various issues)
presentation.defJa: ほかの語の前について、いろいろな、多くのという意味を表す。
presentation.note: A formal prefix typical of newspapers and official writing (諸外国, 諸課題, 諸経費), attached directly to Sino-Japanese nouns with roughly the meaning of いろいろな.

presentation.meaning: there's no point (in ~ing); it can't be helped
presentation.defJa: どうにもならない。また、何かをしても意味がない。
presentation.note: A colloquial contraction of 仕様がない that is very common in speech; しかたがない is the slightly more neutral equivalent, and ～てもしょうがない means 'there's no point in ~'.
collocations: 今さら悩んでもしょうがない
言ってもしょうがない

presentation.defJa: 競技や催しで、よい成績をとった人や当選した人に贈られる品物。
presentation.note: 賞品 is a prize given as goods; prize money is 賞金, and the homophone 商品 means merchandise for sale.

presentation.defJa: 一部を省いて、短くしたり簡単にしたりすること。
presentation.note: A neutral word in both speech and writing for leaving something out or shortening it; the verb 略す is similar but is used especially for abbreviating names and terms.

presentation.defJa: 品物を売る店。特に、おしゃれな店や専門の店。
presentation.note: Common in compounds and for fashionable or specialty stores (ペットショップ, オンラインショップ); the everyday general word is 店.

presentation.defJa: 同じ題名やテーマで、続けて出される本や番組などのひとまとまり。
presentation.note: Used for books, TV programs, products and sporting contests alike; シリーズ化 means turning a single work into an ongoing series.

presentation.defJa: 皮膚や布、紙などが縮んだり折れたりしてできる細い筋。
presentation.note: Used for skin, cloth and paper alike and usually written in kana; 眉間にしわを寄せる describes frowning in displeasure or concentration.

presentation.defJa: 米や果物などから作る、すっぱい味の調味料。
presentation.note: Often said politely as お酢 in everyday speech; 酢の物 refers to vinegared side dishes, a staple of Japanese home cooking.

presentation.defJa: 長い時間、途切れることなく続くようす。「ずっと」を強めた言い方。
presentation.note: A drawn-out, more emotional spoken variant of ずっと that stresses how long something has lasted; it sounds casual and is rare in formal writing.

presentation.defJa: 習い事や技術を教える民間の教室。
presentation.note: Mostly used for private lesson schools in compounds like 英会話スクール or 料理スクール; regular schools are called 学校.

presentation.defJa: 旅客機の中で乗客の世話をする女性の乗務員の、古い呼び方。
presentation.note: Now dated; the standard terms are 客室乗務員 or the abbreviation CA, which also cover male crew.
collocations: スチュワーデスになる
スチュワーデスにあこがれる

presentation.defJa: 余分なものがなく、整っていて気持ちがよいようす。
presentation.note: Describes the pleasant clarity of removing excess, whether in a room, a design, one's mood or a stuffy nose; すっきりしない means something remains unresolved or nagging.

presentation.defJa: 劇場などで、演技や演奏をするための一段高い場所。また、その公演。
presentation.note: Interchangeable with 舞台 for a physical stage, but ステージ is preferred for concerts and pop performances, and it can also mean a stage or phase (次のステージ).

presentation.defJa: 足を包む、薄くてよく伸びる女性用の靴下。
presentation.note: In Japan the word usually means sheer pantyhose; you はく (put on) them, and a run in them is called 伝線.
collocations: ストッキングが伝線する

presentation.defJa: 動いているものや続いている物事が止まること。また、止めること。
presentation.note: A casual, punchy alternative to 停止 or 止まる, common in news headlines and speech for services, production or plans coming to a halt.

presentation.meaning: loudspeaker; (also) a speaker at an event
presentation.defJa: 電気の信号を音に変えて、大きく流す機械。
presentation.note: Primarily means a loudspeaker; for a person who speaks, Japanese more often says 講演者 or 話し手, though スピーカー appears at conferences and events.
collocations: スピーカーから流れる
ワイヤレススピーカー

presentation.defJa: 体つきがすらりとしてかっこいいようす。また、洗練されているようす。
presentation.note: In Japanese it chiefly means slim, or polished and elegant in manner, not intelligent; the English 'clever' sense appears mainly in tech compounds like スマートフォン.

presentation.meaning: sorry; I apologize (plain, mostly male speech)
presentation.defJa: 相手に悪いことをしたと感じて、申し訳なく思う気持ちを表す言葉。
presentation.note: A plain-form apology heard mostly from men or older speakers; すみません is the polite everyday form, and すまないが can open a request like 'sorry, but...'.

presentation.defJa: 発表のときに画面に映して見せる、一枚ごとの資料。
presentation.note: Today it mostly means a presentation slide; as a verb, スライドする means to slide or shift, as when moving a schedule or a pay scale.

presentation.meaning: to shift; to stagger (timing or position)
presentation.defJa: 位置や時間を、少しだけ動かして変える。
presentation.note: Means moving something slightly out of its usual position or time, not necessarily later; for a formal postponement 延期する is used.

presentation.meaning: in a row; lined up in large numbers
presentation.defJa: 多くのものが一列に、または一面に並んでいるようす。
presentation.note: Conveys an impressive number of things or people lined up side by side; ずらっと is a more casual variant.

presentation.defJa: 家の中で履く、かかとの部分がない簡単な履き物。
presentation.note: Slippers are worn indoors in Japanese homes and some schools and offices, often with a separate pair for the toilet; the verb is 履く.
collocations: スリッパに履き替える

presentation.meaning: to print (with a press or plate)
presentation.defJa: 版にインクをつけて、紙に文字や絵を写し取る。
presentation.note: Written 刷る and used for printing with presses or plates, as with newspapers and posters; 印刷する is the general word, and the homophones 擦る (rub) and 掏る (pickpocket) are different verbs.

presentation.defJa: その家族に共通する名前。名字。
presentation.note: A formal word used on forms and in writing (the Civil Code itself says 氏); in conversation people say 名字.

presentation.defJa: そのものがもともと持っている特徴や性格。
presentation.note: Used for the inherent properties of substances as well as the temperament of people or animals; for a person's personality, 性格 is more common in everyday speech.

presentation.defJa: 草や木が育って大きくなること。
presentation.note: Traditionally reserved for plants, while 成長 covers people, animals and economies; many newspapers and textbooks now write 成長 even for plants.

presentation.defJa: 生まれた年と月と日。
presentation.note: A formal compound used on forms, IDs and official documents; in conversation people talk about 誕生日.

presentation.defJa: 休まずに、一生懸命に物事を続けるようす。
presentation.note: Pictures earnest, busy, repeated effort, often on small tasks; こつこつ stresses steady long-term persistence rather than visible bustle.

presentation.meaning: by all means; at any cost (strong wish or request)
presentation.defJa: どんなことがあっても。強く願ったり頼んだりするときに使う。
presentation.note: An emphatic, somewhat formal form of ぜひ, typical of speeches, business requests and earnest appeals.
collocations: ぜひともお願いしたい
ぜひとも実現させたい
ぜひとも参加していただきたい

presentation.defJa: 大学で、教授の指導のもと少人数で研究や発表を行う授業。
presentation.note: Short for ゼミナール (from German Seminar); in Japanese universities a ゼミ is a core small-group class, often tied to the graduation thesis.

presentation.meaning: to attack; to go on the offensive
presentation.defJa: 敵や相手に向かって、勢いよく戦いをしかける。
presentation.note: Used for military, sports and game attacks and figuratively for bold, aggressive approaches (攻めたデザイン); don't confuse it with the homophone 責める, 'to blame'.

presentation.defJa: 石灰石などを焼いて粉にしたもので、水と混ぜると固まる建築の材料。
presentation.note: セメント is the powder binder itself; mixed with sand, gravel and water and left to harden it becomes コンクリート, though everyday speech sometimes blurs the two.

presentation.defJa: 衣類や食器などの汚れを落とすために使う薬剤。
presentation.note: A general word for synthetic cleaning agents for laundry, dishes or surfaces; 石けん (soap) is usually treated as a separate category.

presentation.defJa: 頭から足の先までの、体のすべて。
presentation.note: 全身 refers to the entire physical body (全身麻酔, 全身写真); 全体 is used for the whole of anything, not specifically a body.

presentation.defJa: 長さの単位。一メートルの百分の一。
presentation.note: センチ is the everyday clipped form of センチメートル, used in speech, weather reports and clothing sizes; formal and scientific writing prefers センチメートル or cm.

presentation.defJa: 名詞の前について、「すべての」「全体の」という意味を表す語。
presentation.note: 総 attaches to Sino-Japanese nouns to mean 'total' or 'covering everything' (総額, 総人口, 総会) and belongs to formal, written registers; 全 overlaps but stresses 'every single one' (全国, 全員).

presentation.meaning: softly, gently; quietly (so as not to disturb)
presentation.defJa: 音を立てないように、静かに気をつけて動くようす。
presentation.note: そうっと is a drawn-out, emphatic form of そっと that conveys extra care or tenderness; it is common in speech, picture books and narrative but rare in formal writing.
collocations: そうっとドアを閉める

presentation.meaning: in those days; at that time
presentation.defJa: 話の中で述べた、その時期。当時。
presentation.note: そのころ points back to a period already mentioned and is softer and more conversational than 当時, which sounds more written and documentary.

presentation.defJa: 前に述べたことが理由で、という意味を表すつなぎの言葉。
presentation.note: そのため is a neutral written connector for cause and effect, common in news and explanations, where だから is more conversational; そのためには means 'to that end', and そのために can mark either a cause or a purpose depending on context.

presentation.defJa: タデ科の植物の実をひいた粉で作る、細長い麺。日本の伝統的な食べ物の一つ。
presentation.note: Usually written in hiragana (katakana ソバ for the plant); in other contexts the same sound そば means 'beside, nearby' (側), so context decides.

presentation.defJa: 前のことから考えると当然そうなるはずなのに、実際は違う、という気持ちを表す言葉。
presentation.note: それなのに carries surprise, frustration or reproach that the outcome goes against expectations; しかし or それでも state the contrast more neutrally.
collocations: それなのに平気な顔で

presentation.defJa: 相手の言ったことや前のことを受けて、「もしそうであるなら」という意味でつなぐ言葉。
presentation.note: それなら takes up what was just said and draws a conclusion from it; it is conversational, while それでは or では are a little more formal and だったら more casual.
collocations: それならそうと言ってくれればいいのに

presentation.meaning: that's too bad; I'm sorry to hear that (polite sympathy)
presentation.defJa: 相手の体の具合が悪いことや困ったことを聞いて、心配や同情を伝える丁寧な言い方。
presentation.note: A polite, slightly old-fashioned set response of sympathy to news of illness or trouble; casual speech uses それは大変だね or 大丈夫?, and plain それはいけない can also mean 'that won't do'.
collocations: それはいけませんね。お大事に
それはいけませんでしたね

presentation.defJa: 数字の前について、順番を表す語。
presentation.note: 第 turns a number into an ordinal in formal or written contexts (第2章, 第3条, 第1回); in speech, ～番目 is the everyday way to say 'the Nth'.

presentation.defJa: 車や自転車の車輪の外側につける、ゴムでできた輪。
presentation.note: タイア is an older, rarer spelling; the standard modern form seen everywhere is タイヤ, used for car and bicycle tires alike.

presentation.meaning: in the first place, to begin with; first, foremost
presentation.defJa: ほかの理由よりもまず。何よりも大事な理由を出すときに使う。
presentation.note: As a sentence-opening adverb, often written in kana, だいいち brings in the most decisive reason in an argument or complaint; そもそも is similar but questions the premise itself.
collocations: だいいち、そんな時間はない

presentation.defJa: 二つのものを並べて比べ合わせること。また、比べたときに違いがはっきりしていること。
presentation.note: 対照 means setting two things side by side to bring out their difference (対照的, 'contrasting'); do not confuse it with the homophones 対象 (target, object) and 対称 (symmetry).

presentation.defJa: かなり。程度が進んでいるようす。
presentation.note: Today this adverb is far more often pronounced だいぶ and frequently written in kana; だいぶん is the fuller variant, especially common in western Japan, and as a place name 大分 is read おおいた.

presentation.meaning: title (of a book, film, song, etc.)
presentation.defJa: 本や映画、歌などにつける名前。タイトル。
presentation.note: 題名 is the title of a work such as a book, film or song; タイトル is the everyday loanword and also covers sports titles, while 表題 is more formal and used for documents.

presentation.defJa: 列車の運行を、時刻と駅を軸にした線で表した図。運行計画。
presentation.note: In Japan the word most often means a railway operation chart, and its clipped form ダイヤ is the everyday word for train schedules (ダイヤが乱れる); for diagrams in general, 図 or 図表 is more usual.

presentation.defJa: 炭素だけでできた、最も硬い天然の鉱物。宝石として価値が高い。
presentation.note: Often shortened to ダイヤ in speech and advertising, though ダイヤ can also mean a train schedule (from ダイヤグラム), so context matters.
collocations: ダイヤモンドのように硬い

presentation.defJa: 回したり押したりして、番号や目盛りを合わせるための部分。
presentation.note: Besides the rotary dial of old phones, ダイヤル is used for any turning knob (on a safe, radio or camera), and ダイヤルする still means to place a call.

presentation.defJa: 程度や価値、能力などを上のほうへ引き上げる。
presentation.note: 高める is the transitive partner of 高まる (to rise) and is typical of formal and written Japanese about abstract qualities such as awareness, quality or efficiency; 上げる is more everyday and physical.

presentation.meaning: I'm home; I'm back (greeting on returning)
presentation.defJa: 外から家に帰ったときに、家にいる人に向かって言うあいさつ。
presentation.note: As a greeting it is answered with おかえり(なさい); written 只今 or ただ今 it also means 'right now' or 'just now' in formal announcements (ただいま電話が混み合っております).

presentation.defJa: とても短い時間のうちに。あっという間に。
presentation.note: たちまち stresses how fast something happens, often as a vivid result in narrative or news; すぐに is the plain everyday word and あっという間に more colloquial.

presentation.meaning: to be built, to be erected
presentation.defJa: 建物などが新しくつくられて、その場所に立つ。
presentation.note: 建つ is used only for buildings and structures coming into being; for people or things standing upright the general 立つ is used, and the transitive partner is 建てる.

presentation.defJa: 和服を着るときにはく、親指とほかの指が分かれた布の靴下。
presentation.note: Pairs of tabi are counted with 足 (一足), the reading たび is irregular, and the rubber-soled outdoor version is 地下足袋 (じかたび).

presentation.defJa: 二つ重なること。二倍。また、二人用の大きさのもの。
presentation.note: Used mostly in compounds (ダブルベッド, ダブルチェック, ダブルパンチ) or for a double room; for 'twice the amount' in ordinary speech, 二倍 is more natural.

presentation.defJa: 川の水をせき止めてためるために造った、大きな堤。
presentation.note: ダム covers flood-control, hydroelectric and reservoir dams alike; 堤防 by contrast is an embankment running along a river rather than a barrier across it.

presentation.defJa: どうしようか迷って、なかなか決められない。思い切って行動できない。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (the kanji 躊躇う is rare); the Sino-Japanese 躊躇する (ちゅうちょする) is more formal, and 迷う focuses on being torn between options rather than holding back.
collocations: 口にするのをためらう

presentation.defJa: 身なりや生活、態度などにきちんとしたところがなく、しまりがない。
presentation.note: A critical, fairly colloquial word for sloppiness in appearance, habits, time or money; it sounds harsh when said directly about someone and is stronger than だらけた (slack, lazy).

presentation.defJa: 時間や長さなどがみじかいことを表す語。
presentation.note: A Sino-Japanese prefix read たん that attaches to nouns in everyday compounds such as 短時間, 短期間 and 短距離; on its own, 'short' is the adjective 短い.

presentation.meaning: to tear into pieces (by hand); to pick off
presentation.defJa: 手で細かく引き裂く。また、つまんで取る。
presentation.note: Describes tearing something soft into pieces with the fingers, such as bread, lettuce or paper, and is usually written in kana; 破る is used for ripping or breaking something, often forcefully or by accident.

presentation.meaning: tip, gratuity; chip (e.g. a semiconductor chip)
presentation.defJa: サービスへのお礼として、料金とは別に払うお金。
presentation.note: A loanword covering both a gratuity and a small piece such as a semiconductor or potato chip, with context deciding which; in traditional Japanese inns a tip is politely called 心付け.

presentation.defJa: 黒板に字や絵をかくための、白などの細い棒。
presentation.note: The everyday loanword for blackboard chalk, also used for sidewalk or climbing chalk; the older Japanese word 白墨 survives only in written or nostalgic contexts.

presentation.meaning: occasion, opportunity (to do something while doing something else)
presentation.defJa: ある用事をするときに、それと一緒に別のこともできる機会。
presentation.note: Usually appears as 〜のついでに 'while doing X, on the way'; unlike 機会, it implies the second action is incidental and costs little extra effort.

presentation.defJa: 国や地域で、支払いや売り買いの手段として使われるお金。円やドルなど。
presentation.note: Normally written 通貨, it is the formal economic word for a currency such as the yen or the dollar; do not confuse it with its homophone 通過 'passing through'.

presentation.defJa: 住まいから勤め先へ通うこと。
presentation.note: 通勤 is specifically commuting to a workplace, while 通学 is commuting to school; both take する and appear constantly in news about transport and work styles.

presentation.defJa: ちがう言葉を話す人の間に入って、話を別の言葉に言いかえて伝えること。また、その人。
presentation.note: 通訳 is oral interpreting and also the person who does it, while 翻訳 is written translation; 同時通訳 means simultaneous interpreting.

presentation.meaning: to rank next to; to follow, come after
presentation.defJa: 順位や程度などが、あるもののすぐあとに来る。
presentation.note: A formal, written verb usually in the pattern AはBに次ぐ or Bに次いで, common in rankings and statistics; do not confuse it with 継ぐ 'to inherit' or 注ぐ 'to pour', which share the reading つぐ.

presentation.meaning: to spread, be transmitted (of news, information); to be conveyed
presentation.defJa: 話や知らせ、気持ちなどが、人から人へ広がって届く。
presentation.note: The intransitive partner of 伝える 'to convey'; it covers news spreading, feelings getting across, and traditions being handed down, as in 代々伝わる.

presentation.meaning: to be connected, linked (to); to lead to
presentation.defJa: 離れているもの同士が結びつく。また、ある結果をもたらす。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana in newspapers because 繋 is not a common-use kanji; it is the intransitive partner of つなぐ and also means 'to lead to' a result, as in 事故につながる.

presentation.meaning: to stumble, trip (over something); to suffer a setback
presentation.defJa: 歩いているときに足が物に当たって、転びそうになる。
presentation.note: Takes に for the obstacle (段差につまずく) and is also used figuratively for hitting a setback early on; it is normally written in kana.

presentation.meaning: to pile up, stack; to load
presentation.defJa: 物を上へ上へと重ねて置く。
presentation.note: Means stacking or loading physical things and, figuratively, accumulating experience or practice (経験を積む); the intransitive 積もる is used for snow or dust piling up by itself.

presentation.defJa: 作品や研究、話し合いなどの中心となる題や考え。
presentation.note: A German-derived loanword for the central subject of a work, study or event; it is broader than 題名, which is just a title, and often appears as 〜をテーマに.

presentation.defJa: 値段や程度などがひくいことを表す語。
presentation.note: A Sino-Japanese prefix read てい that forms compounds such as 低価格 and 低気圧; on its own, 'low' is the adjective 低い.

presentation.defJa: 電気が送られてこなくなって、使えなくなること。
presentation.note: The standard word for a power cut in news and everyday speech; a blackout across a whole region is often called 大規模停電.

presentation.defJa: 根拠がなく、いいかげんなこと。また、そのような話。
presentation.note: A blunt word for groundless nonsense or careless, haphazard action, stronger and more accusatory than いいかげん; でたらめに can also simply mean 'at random'.

presentation.defJa: テニスをするために線を引いた、平らな場所。
presentation.note: A straightforward loanword; in casual talk it is often shortened to コート when the sport is clear from context.
collocations: テニスコートを予約する
テニスコートを借りる

presentation.meaning: the same; the said, the aforementioned (prefix, as in 'the company')
presentation.defJa: 前に出てきたものと、おなじものを指す語。
presentation.note: A written-style prefix read どう used mainly in news and reports to refer back to something just mentioned, as in 同社 'the said company' or 同年 'the same year'.

presentation.defJa: お礼を言われたときに、気にしなくていいと伝える言葉。
presentation.note: The textbook reply to thanks, which can sound stiff or distant among friends, where いえいえ or a simple nod is more common.
collocations: いえいえ、どういたしまして
どういたしましてと答える
どういたしましてと返す

presentation.meaning: the East, the Orient (Asia as a cultural sphere)
presentation.defJa: 日本や中国、インドなど、アジアの国々をまとめて指す言葉。西洋と対比して使われる。
presentation.note: A somewhat formal, older-sounding word for Asia as a cultural sphere, used mostly in fixed compounds like 東洋医学 and in contrast with 西洋; in politics and economics アジア is far more common today.

presentation.defJa: 緊張したり期待したりして、心臓の鼓動が速く強くなる様子。
presentation.note: An onomatopoeic word for a racing heart from nerves, excitement or attraction, usually used with する; casual writing often puts it in katakana as ドキドキ.
collocations: どきどきしながら待つ

presentation.defJa: 固いものが熱で液体になる。また、水などにまざって見えなくなる。
presentation.note: Used for melting by heat and dissolving in liquid (砂糖が水に溶ける); the homophone 解ける is used for knots or tension coming loose, and some writers prefer it for snow thawing.

presentation.meaning: all at once, suddenly (of laughter, crowds, fatigue)
presentation.defJa: 大勢の人や物、気持ちなどが、一度にたくさん押し寄せる様子。
presentation.note: Describes something happening in a sudden mass, typically laughter, crowds or fatigue (どっと疲れが出る); it adds a sense of volume that 急に lacks.
collocations: 人がどっと押し寄せる

presentation.meaning: to put (someone) up for the night, to lodge
presentation.defJa: 人を自分の家などで寝させて、一晩過ごさせる。
presentation.note: The transitive counterpart of 泊まる 'to stay overnight': 泊める means letting someone else stay, and it should not be confused with 止める 'to stop', also read とめる.

presentation.meaning: anyway, at any rate; setting aside (X)
presentation.defJa: 細かいことは別にして。何はさておき。
presentation.note: Used to cut through deliberation and move to what matters, and in Xはともかく 'X aside'; it is close to とにかく, which is more colloquial and more common in speech.

presentation.defJa: 石油などから作られる、軽くて丈夫な合成繊維。
presentation.note: A loanword used for the material itself, as in product labels like ナイロン製; in some regions ナイロン袋 also loosely means any plastic bag.
collocations: ナイロンのストッキング

presentation.defJa: 入れ物の中に入っているもの。また、見た目ではない実質。
presentation.note: Refers to what is inside a container and, figuratively, to real substance as opposed to appearance (見た目より中身); 内容 is the more formal word for the content of a talk or document.

presentation.defJa: こぶしや棒などで、人を強く打つ。
presentation.note: A direct, physical verb for hitting someone with a fist or object, common in crime reports; 叩く is broader and lighter, covering pats, slaps and striking objects.

presentation.meaning: after all, you see (giving an emphatic reason); at any rate
presentation.defJa: ほかのことはさておき、とにかく。理由を強く言うときに使う。
presentation.note: A conversational adverb that stresses an overriding reason, typically followed by のだ or から; it is close to とにかく but more often explains why something happened, and is also written 何しろ.
collocations: なにしろ初めてなので

presentation.meaning: to bear fruit; (of fruit) to grow on a plant
presentation.defJa: 草や木に実ができる。
presentation.note: Almost always written in kana with 実 or a fruit as the subject, so context separates it from なる 'to become'; it is plainer than 実る, which stresses ripening and a successful harvest.

presentation.meaning: somehow; for no particular reason; vaguely
presentation.defJa: はっきりした理由はないが、何かそう感じられるようす。
presentation.note: Casual but fine in essays, it marks a vague feeling with no clear cause; なぜか, by contrast, puts more weight on puzzlement about why.

presentation.meaning: indescribably, truly (before adjectives); (not) at all (with a negative)
presentation.defJa: 言葉では言い表せないほど。本当に。
presentation.note: With a negative (なんとも思わない) it means 'not in the least', while before an adjective it adds an emotional 'truly, indescribably'; なんとも言えない is by far the most frequent set phrase.

presentation.meaning: number; especially a car's license plate number
presentation.defJa: 番号。特に、車につけられた登録番号の札。
presentation.note: In everyday speech ナンバー often means a car's license plate, while 番号 is the normal word for ID or phone numbers; ナンバー also appears in loan compounds like ナンバーワン.

presentation.meaning: smiling cheerfully; with a beaming smile
presentation.defJa: うれしそうに、声を出さずに笑うようす。
presentation.note: A warm mimetic word for a gentle, sustained smile without laughing aloud; にやにや, by contrast, suggests a smirk or knowing grin.

presentation.meaning: to simmer; to boil or stew (food in seasoned liquid)
presentation.defJa: 食べ物を水やだしなどに入れて火にかけ、熱を通す。
presentation.note: Means cooking food in liquid so it takes on flavor, as in 煮物; ゆでる is boiling in plain water, and 炊く is used for rice or, in western Japan, for simmered dishes too.
collocations: 煮ても焼いても食えない

presentation.defJa: らせん状の溝がついていて、回して物を締めつけたり固定したりする部品。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (螺子 or 捻子 are rare); ねじを巻く literally means winding a clockwork but is also used figuratively for spurring someone on.

presentation.defJa: 首にかけて身につける飾り。
presentation.note: The everyday word for any necklace; 首飾り is the native equivalent but sounds old-fashioned or literary, while ペンダント refers to one with a hanging pendant.

presentation.defJa: 細かいぎざぎざの刃を前後に動かして、木などを切る道具。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (the kanji 鋸 is rare), and the verb is 引く because traditional Japanese saws cut on the pull stroke.

presentation.defJa: 動きがとても遅いようす。
presentation.note: Carries a mildly impatient tone about something moving annoyingly slowly, whereas ゆっくり is neutral; のろのろ運転 is a stock phrase in traffic reports.

presentation.defJa: 相手の言葉に答えたり、同意したりするときに使う返事の言葉。
presentation.note: The standard polite 'yes' (ええ is softer, うん casual), but in conversation it often signals attention rather than agreement, and a doubled はいはい can sound dismissive.

presentation.defJa: 別れるときに言う、くだけたあいさつの言葉。
presentation.note: Casual and childlike, used with children or close friends; adults talking to peers more often say じゃあね or またね, and さようなら is more formal.

presentation.meaning: absurd; ridiculous; not worth taking seriously
presentation.defJa: まじめにするのがおかしいと思うほど、意味や価値がない。
presentation.note: Says something is too pointless to take seriously; ばかばかしい is a more emphatic form, while くだらない focuses on worthlessness or triviality.
collocations: ばからしくてやっていられない

presentation.defJa: ほうきなどで、ごみや落ち葉を払って集める。
presentation.note: Specifically sweeping with a broom, whereas 掃除する is general cleaning; 掃いて捨てるほど is an idiom for 'a dime a dozen', and the homophones 履く and 吐く must be told apart by kanji.
collocations: 掃いて捨てるほどある

presentation.defJa: 水などを入れて運ぶ、取っ手のついた入れ物。
presentation.note: The everyday word for a bucket, from English 'bucket'; the idiom バケツをひっくり返したような雨 describes a torrential downpour.
collocations: バケツをひっくり返したような雨

presentation.meaning: How do you do; nice to meet you
presentation.defJa: 初めて会った人にするあいさつの言葉。
presentation.note: Used only at a first meeting and usually followed by one's name and よろしくお願いします; it is neutral-polite and works in both business and casual introductions.
collocations: はじめまして、よろしくお願いします
はじめましてのあいさつ

presentation.defJa: くり返し現れる型や傾向。
presentation.note: A broad loanword for a recurring design, behavior or regularity; 型 is the native counterpart, and いつものパターン colloquially means 'the same old story'.

presentation.meaning: cross mark, meaning wrong or no
presentation.defJa: 間違いや不可を表す、二本の線を斜めに交差させた印。
presentation.note: Read ばつ and often written バツ in kana; in Japan it marks 'wrong' or 'no' as the opposite of ○ (まる), and colloquial バツイチ means 'divorced once'.

presentation.defJa: 車などを後ろへ動かすこと。また、うしろや背景。
presentation.note: When driving, バック means moving in reverse (バックする/させる), while elsewhere it can mean background or backing (バックに流れる音楽); don't confuse it with バッグ 'bag'.

presentation.defJa: 押したり引いたりすると元に戻ろうとする、金属などで作った部品。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (発条 is rare); besides the mechanical part it is used for athletic springiness and in 〜をばねにする, 'to use something as a springboard'.

presentation.meaning: to put on (a ring, gloves); to fit into
presentation.defJa: 指輪や手袋などを、ぴったり合うように身につける。また、穴や枠に入れる。
presentation.note: Used for things that fit snugly on a body part (rings, gloves, watches) or into a slot; colloquially 人をはめる means 'to set someone up', and 型にはめる means to force into a mold.

presentation.defJa: 「…に逆らう」「…と対立する」という意味をそえる語。
presentation.note: Attaches to Sino-Japanese nouns to express opposition or reversal (反戦, 反作用), whereas 非 and 不 simply negate ('non-', 'un-') and 無 expresses absence.

presentation.defJa: 下着として腰から下にはく衣類。ファッションではズボンのこともいう。
presentation.note: In everyday speech パンツ usually means underwear, especially for children or men, but in fashion writing it means trousers, as in ワイドパンツ, so context decides.

presentation.defJa: いっしょに音楽を演奏するグループ。また、物を締めるための帯。
presentation.note: Most often a pop or rock group (バンドを組む 'to form a band'), but it also covers straps and belts such as 時計のバンド or ヘアバンド.

presentation.defJa: 車や自転車の向きを変えるために、手で握って操作する部分。
presentation.note: In Japanese it chiefly means a steering wheel or bicycle handlebars, while a door handle is more often 取っ手 or ドアノブ, and ハンドルを握る can simply mean 'to drive'.

presentation.defJa: 「…ではない」という否定の意味をそえる語。
presentation.note: Prefixes Sino-Japanese nouns to mean 'not X' (非公式, 非常識); which word takes 非, 不 or 無 is fixed by convention, and 反 means 'against' rather than simply 'not'.

presentation.defJa: よく光ってつやがあるようす。また、真新しいようす。
presentation.note: Describes a glossy, polished shine and by extension anything brand-new, as in ぴかぴかの一年生; きらきら suggests twinkling light, like stars, rather than a polished surface.

presentation.defJa: 片手で持って撃つ小型の銃。
presentation.note: A slightly dated everyday word for a handgun (news reports prefer 拳銃 or 銃), but it remains the usual word for a starter's pistol in sports.

presentation.defJa: 体の働きを整えるために欠かせない栄養素の一つ。
presentation.note: A neutral everyday and scientific term from German 'Vitamin'; the usual verb is とる (摂る), the standard verb for taking in nutrients.

presentation.defJa: 少しのずれもなく、よく合うようす。また、急に止まるようす。
presentation.note: Crisper and slightly more written than ぴったり, the more common conversational form; ぴたりと止む is typical for something stopping all at once.

presentation.meaning: one; a single, brief ~ (prefix on native words, e.g. 'a breather')
presentation.defJa: 名詞の前について、「ひとつの」「少しの」という意味を加える語。
presentation.note: The native reading ひと~ attaches to native words such as 一息, 一晩 and 一言 and often softens the sense to 'a bit of', whereas いち~ goes with Sino-Japanese compounds such as 一回 and 一部.

presentation.meaning: for the time being; for now (provisionally)
presentation.defJa: 完全ではないが、とりあえず。今のところは。
presentation.note: Close to とりあえず but a little more written; it marks a provisional resting point with more to come, and is common in news phrases such as ひとまず安心 and ひとまず決着.

presentation.meaning: by itself; of its own accord; spontaneously
presentation.defJa: 誰も何もしないのに、自然にそうなる様子。
presentation.note: Describes something happening with no apparent agent, from doors swinging open to tears welling up; 自然に is broader and more neutral, while 自動的に implies a mechanism.
collocations: ドアがひとりでに開く

presentation.defJa: 薄くて水を通さない、やわらかい合成樹脂。袋や傘などに使われる。
presentation.note: In everyday Japanese ビニール loosely covers thin, soft plastic film of any kind, not just PVC, while hard plastic items are called プラスチック.

presentation.defJa: 温度を下げて、つめたくする。
presentation.note: The transitive partner of 冷える; besides literal cooling it appears in idioms such as 頭を冷やす 'to calm down' and 肝を冷やす 'to be terrified'.

presentation.defJa: あらゆる分野の知識を項目ごとにまとめて解説した本。
presentation.note: Normally written 百科事典; 事典 explains things and facts while 辞典 explains words, though the two are often confused because they share the reading じてん.

presentation.meaning: building (especially a large multistory office building)
presentation.defJa: 何階もある大きな建物。特に事務所などが入る高い建物。
presentation.note: In everyday speech the clipped form ビル is used almost exclusively; the full ビルディング survives mainly in formal or historical writing and in the names of buildings.
collocations: オフィスビルディング
ビルディングを建設する

presentation.meaning: to expand; to widen; to spread out (unfold)
presentation.defJa: 範囲や規模を大きくする。たたんである物を開く。
presentation.note: The transitive partner of 広がる; it covers both physically unfolding things (地図や傘を広げる) and widening a scope, where 拡大する is the more formal Sino-Japanese equivalent.

presentation.defJa: 赤に白をまぜたような、明るくやわらかい色。もも色。
presentation.note: Used as a noun with の or 色 (ピンクのシャツ, ピンク色); the native 桃色 sounds old-fashioned, and ピンク can also hint at 'erotic', as in ピンク映画.

presentation.defJa: 服やかばんの口を、金具を引いて開けたり閉めたりする仕組み。
presentation.note: ファスナー, ジッパー and the colloquial チャック all mean zipper; ファスナー is the standard term in shops and manufacturing.
collocations: ファスナー付きのポーチ

presentation.meaning: to include (in a total or group)
presentation.defJa: あるものを全体の中に入れて、いっしょに数えたり扱ったりする。
presentation.note: Normally written 含める; it stresses the deliberate act of counting something in (often as ～を含めて), whereas 含む more often states what something contains, as in ビタミンを含む.

presentation.meaning: to fool around; to joke; to mess about
presentation.defJa: まじめにせず、冗談を言ったり遊び半分の行動をしたりする。
presentation.note: Usually describes playful or silly behavior, especially by children; in the angry phrase ふざけるな it means 'don't mess with me' or 'are you kidding me', so tone matters.

presentation.meaning: suspension of service; being cut off (of transport or communication lines)
presentation.defJa: 電車や道路、電話などが通じなくなること。
presentation.note: A news-style word for transport or communication lines being cut off; do not confuse it with its homophone 普通 'ordinary', and note 音信不通 for losing contact with a person.

presentation.defJa: 小さな声で、不満などを続けて言う様子。
presentation.note: An onomatopoeic word for muttering complaints under one's breath, usually with 言う; as a noun it can also mean small bumps or a rash on the skin.
collocations: ぶつぶつと独り言を言う

presentation.defJa: 柄のついた浅くて平らな鍋。焼いたりいためたりするのに使う。
presentation.note: The everyday word for a frying pan; a Chinese wok is 中華鍋, and 鍋 on its own usually suggests a deeper pot.
collocations: フッ素加工のフライパン

presentation.defJa: 女性や子どもが着る、薄い布で作られたシャツのような上着。
presentation.note: In Japanese ブラウス is reserved for women's and girls' shirts; a man's dress shirt is a ワイシャツ or simply シャツ.

presentation.meaning: to hang (so it dangles); to carry dangling from the hand
presentation.defJa: 物の上の部分を留めて、下にたれるようにつるす。手に下げて持つ。
presentation.note: Usually written ぶら下げる; it emphasizes something hanging loosely or being carried casually (袋をぶら下げて歩く), whereas 吊るす is more neutral and 掛ける implies hooking onto something.

presentation.defJa: 毛を束ねて柄に植えた道具。汚れを落としたり、髪をとかしたりするのに使う。
presentation.note: Covers any brush for cleaning or grooming, such as 歯ブラシ and ヘアブラシ; a brush for painting or calligraphy is 筆 or 刷毛 instead.

presentation.defJa: 駅で、乗客が電車に乗り降りするために線路にそって高く作られた場所。
presentation.note: In everyday speech it is shortened to ホーム, while the spelling プラットフォーム is used for the IT and business sense of 'platform'.
collocations: プラットホームに立つ
プラットホームから転落する

presentation.defJa: 会社などに所属せず、自分で仕事を受けて働くこと。また、制限がないこと。
presentation.note: On its own フリー most often means freelance (フリーになる) or 'free of' in compounds like バリアフリー; 'free of charge' is usually 無料, apart from set loanwords such as フリーペーパー.

presentation.defJa: 印刷して配る紙。また、印刷すること。
presentation.note: In schools and offices プリント most often means a printed handout or worksheet; it also covers printing itself and printed fabric patterns (花柄のプリント).

presentation.meaning: old; used; second-hand (prefix on native words, e.g. 'used clothing')
presentation.defJa: 名詞の前について、「年月がたった」「一度使われた」という意味を加える語。
presentation.note: The native reading ふる~ attaches to everyday words (古着, 古本, 古巣) with the sense 'second-hand' or 'long-standing', whereas the reading こ~ appears in formal compounds such as 古代 and 古典.

presentation.defJa: 生まれ育った土地。
presentation.note: 故郷 can be read こきょう (neutral, written) or ふるさと (warm and nostalgic, common in songs and essays); ふるさと納税 is usually written in kana.

presentation.defJa: 服の胸元などにピンで留めて飾るアクセサリー。
presentation.note: A purely decorative pin-on ornament, unlike a バッジ, which usually shows identity, membership or support for a cause.

presentation.defJa: 軽くてやわらかい様子。また、空中にただよう様子。
presentation.note: An onomatopoeic word for airy softness in food, fabric, hair and clouds, used as ふわふわの, ふわふわした or ふわふわと; said of a person or mood it suggests flightiness or dreamy unfocus.

presentation.defJa: おなかの真ん中にある小さなくぼみ。
presentation.note: Usually said with the polite お as おへそ in everyday speech, and found in idioms such as へそを曲げる 'to sulk' and へそくり 'secret savings'.

presentation.defJa: 大きな羽を回して、まっすぐ上がったり空中に止まったりできる航空機。
presentation.note: Commonly shortened to ヘリ in speech and compounds such as ドクターヘリ and ヘリポート; the full form is typical of news and formal writing.
collocations: ヘリコプターが着陸する

presentation.defJa: 針金を曲げたり切ったり、物をはさんだりするのに使う工具。
presentation.note: Comes from English 'pinchers' and means pliers in general; a tool made only for cutting wire is a ニッパー.

presentation.meaning: bonus (especially the seasonal bonus paid twice a year)
presentation.defJa: 毎月の給料とは別に、夏や冬などに支払われるお金。
presentation.note: In Japan ボーナス usually means the summer and winter bonuses that form a regular part of annual pay rather than a reward for exceptional performance; the formal term is 賞与.

presentation.meaning: anti-; prevention of ~; protection against ~ (prefix, e.g. 'disaster prevention')
presentation.defJa: 名詞の前について、それが起きたり入り込んだりしないように守る、という意味を加える語。
presentation.note: Forms Sino-Japanese compounds such as 防災, 防犯, 防水 and 防音, meaning guarding against or keeping out the thing named; compare 耐~ (耐水, 耐震), which means withstanding it rather than keeping it out.

presentation.defJa: 品物を紙や箱、袋などで包むこと。また、その包み。
presentation.note: 包装 is the standard word for packaging and gift-wrapping in shops and business; 梱包 specifically means packing goods for shipment, and ラッピング suggests decorative gift wrap.

presentation.defJa: 宣伝や案内のために、壁などにはる大きな紙。絵や文字がかかれている。
presentation.note: The usual verbs are 貼る (put up) and はがす (take down); a small flyer handed out or delivered is a チラシ rather than a ポスター.

presentation.defJa: 古くなって破れたり、すり切れたりした布や衣服。
presentation.note: Besides literal rags, ぼろ appears in the idiom ぼろが出る (one's flaws or lies come to light), and the casual adjective ぼろい means shabby or run-down.

presentation.defJa: 数や量、程度がとても少ないことを強めて表す。わずかな。
presentation.note: Always placed directly before a noun or quantity to stress how small it is, with a softer, more subjective feel than わずか; it also appears in the modest gift phrase ほんの気持ちです.

presentation.defJa: とても良いわけではないが、悪くもないようす。
presentation.note: Signals lukewarm, moderate approval and can sound mildly negative depending on tone; as an interjection, まあまあ is also used to calm someone down, like 'now, now'.

presentation.meaning: to wind; to coil; to wrap around
presentation.defJa: 細長いものを、ほかの物のまわりにぐるぐると回してつける。また、うずの形になる。
presentation.note: Normally written 巻く; the kana spelling まく is ambiguous with 撒く (to scatter) and 蒔く (to sow seeds), so context or kanji decides the meaning.

presentation.defJa: ちがうものがいっしょになって、一つになる。
presentation.note: Usually written 混ざる; it stresses blending into one uniform whole, while 混じる more often suggests something mixed in yet still noticeable, and the transitive partner is 混ぜる.

presentation.meaning: to be mixed in; to mingle with
presentation.defJa: あるものの中に、ちがうものが入りこんでいる。
presentation.note: Written 混じる when substances blend and 交じる when distinct items, such as people in a group, stay separate; compared with 混ざる it often implies a small admixture that remains distinguishable.

presentation.defJa: 鼻と口をおおう布や紙。病気や花粉、寒さなどを防ぐために使う。
presentation.note: In everyday Japanese マスク almost always means a face mask over the nose and mouth; a mask covering the whole face, as at a festival or in a play, is usually お面 or 仮面.

presentation.defJa: ちがうものをいっしょにして、一つにする。また、ものの中にほかのものを加える。
presentation.note: Transitive partner of 混ざる and 混じる; the kanji 交ぜる is reserved for combining things that stay distinct, as in 冗談を交ぜる, while 混ぜる is for blending into one.

presentation.meaning: to step over; to straddle; (figuratively) to span across
presentation.defJa: 足を大きく開いて、物の上を越える。また、ある境を越えて広がる。
presentation.note: Literally to step over something in one stride; in the news it often means crossing or spanning a boundary, as in 県をまたぐ移動, and the kanji 跨ぐ is rarely used.

presentation.defJa: 目をおおって、開けたり閉じたりする皮膚の部分。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana since the kanji 瞼 is uncommon; まぶたが重い means feeling sleepy, and まぶたに浮かぶ means a scene comes vividly to mind.

presentation.defJa: 寒さを防ぐために首にまく、細長い布。
presentation.note: マフラー is the everyday word for a warm winter scarf, while a light fashion scarf is a スカーフ or ストール; on a car, マフラー also means the exhaust muffler.

presentation.defJa: 四十二・一九五キロメートルを走る長距離の競走。
presentation.note: Strictly the 42.195 km race (a half is ハーフマラソン), but マラソン is also used loosely for any long, grueling effort, as in マラソン交渉.

presentation.defJa: 鉄筋コンクリートなどで造られた、何階もある集合住宅。
presentation.note: In Japanese マンション means a condominium or mid- to high-rise apartment building, often owner-occupied, not a luxury mansion; a cheaper low-rise building is an アパート.

presentation.meaning: not yet; un- (marks something not yet done or reached)
presentation.defJa: まだそうなっていない、という意味を表す。
presentation.note: Attaches to Sino-Japanese nouns to mean 'not yet', implying the state may still change, unlike 不 or 非, which simply negate.

presentation.defJa: 見ていられないほどかわいそうで、情けないようす。
presentation.note: Describes a humiliating, pitiable state that wounds one's pride, often felt about oneself; かわいそう expresses sympathy for others rather than this sense of shame.

presentation.defJa: 布を縫うための機械。
presentation.note: The usual verb is かける, as in ミシンをかける (to sew on a machine); though it comes from English 'machine', in Japanese it refers only to a sewing machine.

presentation.defJa: 長さなどの単位で、一メートルの千分の一。また、千分の一を表す。
presentation.note: Used alone it almost always means millimeters (rainfall is reported in ミリ), while as a prefix it forms units like ミリリットル and ミリ秒; casual 一ミリも～ない means 'not one bit'.

presentation.defJa: 国の主権が国民にあり、国民の意思にもとづいて政治を行うこと。
presentation.note: Rarely used on its own; it appears mostly in compounds such as 民主主義 (democracy), 民主化 (democratization) and 民主的 (democratic).

presentation.defJa: 湿気が多くて、むっとするように暑い。
presentation.note: Describes the humid, sticky heat typical of the Japanese rainy season and summer, whereas plain 暑い is any heat and 暑苦しい stresses stifling, oppressive discomfort.

presentation.defJa: 品詞の一つで、人や物、ことがらの名前を表す言葉。
presentation.note: A grammar term used in school and linguistics; it sounds exactly like 名刺 (business card), so context or the kanji tells them apart.

presentation.defJa: 名前や会社名、連絡先などを印刷した小さなカード。
presentation.note: 名刺交換 is a ritualized part of Japanese business etiquette; the word is a homophone of 名詞 (noun).

presentation.meaning: messed up; ruined, in a shambles; absurd
presentation.defJa: ひどく乱れて、元の形がわからないほどになるようす。
presentation.note: Casual and conversational; besides 'wrecked' or 'unreasonable', it is widely used as an intensifier meaning 'extremely', as in めちゃくちゃおいしい, often shortened to めっちゃ.

presentation.meaning: noticeably; markedly (of a change over time)
presentation.defJa: 変化がはっきりと目立つようす。
presentation.note: Used for a clear change in state, typically a decline or a seasonal shift as in めっきり秋らしくなった; ずいぶん is a broader near-synonym.

presentation.defJa: 喜び祝うのにふさわしいようす。
presentation.note: Often heard as polite おめでたい or adverbially as めでたく ('happily, successfully'); おめでたい人 can also ironically mean a naive, gullible person.

presentation.defJa: 料理や飲み物の名前と値段を並べて書いた一覧。
presentation.note: Besides a restaurant menu, メニュー also means a program or line-up, as in トレーニングメニュー, and a menu in software.

presentation.defJa: 目が回るように感じたり、体がふらついたりすること。
presentation.note: A general word for dizziness or vertigo, usually written in kana (目まい and 眩暈 also occur); the brief lightheadedness on standing up is more specifically called 立ちくらみ.

presentation.defJa: 人と直接会って話をし、その人の人柄や能力を確かめること。
presentation.note: 面接 is an evaluative interview for a job or admission, whereas a journalist's interview is インタビュー or 取材.

presentation.defJa: 電気などの力で軸を回し、機械を動かす装置。
presentation.note: Usually means an electric motor; in compounds such as モーターショー or モータースポーツ it refers to motor vehicles more broadly.

presentation.defJa: ひょっとすると。確かではないが、そうである可能性があると考えるようす。
presentation.note: Conversational but common in writing too; it typically pairs with かもしれない. もしかすると is a slightly more formal variant, and ひょっとしたら is a close synonym.
collocations: もしかしたら～かもしれない

presentation.meaning: to lean on; to lean against
presentation.defJa: 体の重みを壁や物などにあずけて寄りかかる。
presentation.note: Means resting one's weight against something, close to 寄りかかる; 胃がもたれる (a heavy stomach after rich food) is a very common second use.

presentation.defJa: 新しい時代の感覚にあっていて、しゃれているようす。
presentation.note: Describes a style or taste rather than mere newness, often with a stylish, urban nuance; 現代的 is the plainer native equivalent.

presentation.defJa: 服などを着て見せたり、写真にとられたりする仕事をする人。
presentation.note: Besides a fashion model, モデル commonly means a model case, a scale model or a product version (新モデル), so context decides the sense.

presentation.defJa: 一本のレールの上や下を走る鉄道。
presentation.note: A neutral loanword; in Japan monorails are typically elevated lines linking airports, suburbs or theme parks to rail hubs.

presentation.defJa: 物に火をつけて焼く。また、情熱などの感情を高ぶらせる。
presentation.note: The transitive partner of 燃える, normally written 燃やす; it is also used figuratively for passion or fighting spirit, whereas 焼く leans toward cooking or burning something down.

presentation.defJa: 細かいことまで厳しく言うようす。また、音や声がうるさいようす。
presentation.note: In the sense of fussy it takes に (味にやかましい) and suggests someone who nags about details; in the sense of noisy it is close to うるさい but sounds a little more old-fashioned.

presentation.defJa: 湯をわかすための、注ぎ口と取っ手のついた金属の入れ物。
presentation.note: Usually written in kana (薬缶 is rare) and refers to a stovetop kettle; an electric kettle is 電気ケトル, while 電気ポット is a pot that keeps water hot.

presentation.meaning: to beat; to defeat soundly; to knock out (a task)
presentation.defJa: 相手をひどく負かす。また、仕事などを手早く終わらせる。
presentation.note: Casual in tone and suggests beating someone soundly; formal reports prefer 破る or 下す, and やっつけ仕事 means slapdash, rushed work.

presentation.defJa: いろいろ考えたが、結局は。また、思っていたとおり。
presentation.note: The casual spoken form of やはり; it marks a return to an earlier thought or a confirmed expectation, and やはり is preferred in formal writing.

presentation.defJa: 物を入れておくための入れ物。
presentation.note: A somewhat formal, general term common on product labels and in the news; 入れ物 is the casual everyday equivalent.

presentation.meaning: the next; the following (day, year, etc.)
presentation.defJa: 日・朝・年などの前について、「その次の」という意味を表すことば。
presentation.note: Attaches to time words and dates (翌日, 翌朝, 翌年, 翌三日) and counts forward from a reference point already given, whereas 明日 and 来年 count from today.

presentation.meaning: to send (to me or us); to hand over
presentation.defJa: 相手がこちらへ物や手紙、人などを送ってくる。
presentation.note: Always means sending toward the speaker's side and sounds casual, sometimes a little brusque; the neutral equivalent is 送ってくる or くれる.

presentation.meaning: to make dirty; to soil; to pollute
presentation.defJa: きれいなものを、きたなくする。
